chosen.poseName: local +x down (gusset end face on the bed)
chosen.why: The gusset end face on the bed, as the V1.22 base and the 10/07 candidate: the motor mating face, the four output seats and the cut face stand vertical. Bambu: every MUST face clean.
chosen.objectSettingsReason: pipeline R1 brim rule (objectSettingsSource in the slices)

Bambu.objectSettingsSource: R1 default: tip angle 2.4 deg < 10 deg, outer brim

Elegoo.objectSettingsSource: R1 default: tip angle 2.4 deg < 10 deg, outer brim

chosen.mustExplanation: Bambu: every MUST face clean. Elegoo only: Orca's tree support reaches into the d4.4 counterbores of the motor-output screws from the plate exterior and touches 1.1 (left) / 9.7 (right) mm2 of the seat floors, plus 0.3 mm2 of the motor face and 1.3 / 2.4 mm2 of the cut face. On an Elegoo print, pull the tips out of the four counterbores with tweezers so the M2 x 4 heads sit flat. A teardrop roof on these holes was rejected: on the hole beside the shaft the roof would point at the d5 centre aperture and leave 0.4 mm of wall (stock 1.3 mm).

brim.brimInsideHullAllowanceReason: The gusset end face on the bed carries the real 12 x 1.1 mm recess of the stock bracket (community-66/64 notch beside the gusset hole); the outer half keeps part of it. Bambu Studio loops the 4 mm outer brim into it: 2.4 mm2 inside the convex outline on both outer halves, a strip bonded on three sides, cut it out with a blade. Orca puts support feet there instead. Same notch as the V1.22 bases (13.3 mm2 there). Not an opening filled with brim.

rejected.-x down (left): Bambu: 7.6 mm2 of support on the motor mating face; Elegoo: 7.8 mm2 on the output seats (slices/left_outer/mx-down).
rejected.+-z down: the motor face or the four output seats face down onto support 2-3 mm above the bed; the plate exterior is 7 deg off the shaft.
rejected.-y down: the foot-block underside has no flat face (prepare finds no planar contact).

chosen.poseName: local +x down (toe end on the bed, shaft flat, round bore)
chosen.why: Shawn 2026-10-20 on the printed V1.24 teardrop: the d15 pocket and the d14 lip bore stay round and support may stand in the hole. The half stands on its toe end (the stock face that carries the cut gusset; the same pose as the outer half), so the shaft lies flat and the bore's top in print is its heel side on the robot. The support inside the bore touches that heel-side band; the bore's lower side, which carries the robot's weight, prints as a vertical wall with no support on it.
chosen.objectSettingsReason: pipeline R1 brim rule (objectSettingsSource in the slices)

Bambu.objectSettingsSource: R1 default: tip angle 1.8 deg < 10 deg, outer brim

Elegoo.objectSettingsSource: R1 default: tip angle 1.8 deg < 10 deg, outer brim

chosen.mustExplanation: By Shawn's decision, support stands inside the bore: Bambu 11.3 mm2 of the d15 pocket wall (197.2 mm of support inside), 1.3 mm2 of the capture lip, 0.9 mm2 of the lip bore; Elegoo 14.3 mm2 of the pocket wall (766.5 mm inside), 3.9 mm2 of the capture lip, 10.8 mm2 of the lip bore (133.6 mm inside), 2.4 mm2 of the cut face, and 2.5 mm2 of the toe-screw countersink (51.8 mm inside). All of it is on the heel side of the bore, away from the weight side. Break the support out of the bore, then scrape the pocket wall and the lip face smooth until the black sleeve turns freely; on an Elegoo print pick the tips out of the toe countersink so the M2 x 6 head sits flat. The cut face meets the other half across 0.2 mm.

brim.brimInsideHullAllowanceReason: The gusset end face on the bed carries the real 12 x 1.1 mm recess of the stock bracket (community-66/64 notch beside the gusset hole); the inner half keeps the other part of it on the same end face. Bambu Studio loops the 4 mm outer brim into it: 2.4 mm2 inside the convex outline, a strip bonded on three sides, cut it out with a blade. Orca puts support feet there instead. Same notch as the V1.22 bases (13.3 mm2 there). Not an opening filled with brim.

rejected.-x down (heel end on the bed): Bambu 12.8 mm2 of the pocket wall and 276 mm of support inside, Elegoo 21.1 mm2 and 527 mm inside plus 354 mm in the lip bore; Elegoo also loops the brim into the stock notch (slices/left_inner/mx-down).
rejected.heel chamfer down with a round bore: the bore's top in print would be its toe-down side on the robot, so the support scar would sit in the band that takes the robot's weight and push-off.
rejected.heel chamfer down with the 45 deg teardr: printed 2026-10-20; Shawn wants a round bore (slices/*_inner/heel-down hold that study, on the teardrop STL).
rejected.-z down (cut face on the bed): the plate inner face overhangs 15 mm and its support fills the pocket: 64.7 mm2 of the pocket wall and all 22.8 mm2 of the capture lip on support, 869 mm inside (Bambu).
rejected.+z / tilted exterior down: the 1.2 mm sleeve lip ring stands proud of the 7 deg exterior, so no flat face is lowest.
